capabilities.name: list_identity_broadcast
capabilities.description: Send the connectionless List Identity request (encapsulation command 0x63) to UDP/44818 and parse the CIP Identity Object item (0x000C) — vendor_id, device_type, product_code, revision, status, serial_number, product_name, state — the definitive presence/fingerprint for an ODVA device.
capabilities.protocol_reference: ODVA Vol 2 (EtherNet/IP Adaptation of CIP), §2-4.4 (List Identity) and §5-2.2 (Identity Object 0x01)
capabilities.notes: Works with zero session state; the single most useful probe. Also succeeds over TCP/44818 for units that block the UDP variant.

capabilities.name: list_services_enum
capabilities.description: Send List Services (command 0x0004) over TCP/44818 to enumerate the encapsulation services the endpoint supports — the presence of the 'Communications' capability with the CIP-encapsulation flag confirms explicit-messaging is possible, and its absence flags a pure I/O adapter.
capabilities.notes: Cheap follow-on to List Identity; result gates whether the CIP-messaging probes below are worth trying.

capabilities.name: list_interfaces_enum
capabilities.description: Send List Interfaces (command 0x0064) to enumerate the target's non-CIP interfaces — a device answering with multiple interfaces is typically a communications gateway/bridge (rack chassis backplane), a strong signal of a deeper OT segment reachable via CIP routing.

capabilities.name: register_session
capabilities.description: Open a CIP explicit-messaging session with RegisterSession (0x0065) — succeeds with no credentials on any stock EtherNet/IP device and returns a session handle used for every subsequent Unconnected Send / SendRRData request; the fact that it succeeds is itself a finding on segments that shouldn't host OT.

capabilities.name: cip_identity_object_read
capabilities.description: Over the session, issue GetAttributesAll (service 0x01) on Identity Object class 0x01 instance 1 via SendRRData/UnconnectedSend to pull the same identity payload plus device Status word and Major/Minor Recoverable Faults — reveals whether the PLC is in Run/Program/Fault mode.

capabilities.name: cip_tcpip_object_read
capabilities.description: GetAttributesAll on TCP/IP Interface Object (class 0xF5, instance 1) exposes the device's static/DHCP config, IP address, netmask, gateway, primary/secondary name-server, domain name and host name — high-value host/network intelligence pulled with no auth.

capabilities.name: cip_ethernet_link_read
capabilities.description: GetAttributesAll on Ethernet Link Object (class 0xF6) enumerates each physical port's MAC address, link speed/duplex and interface counters — the MAC is a durable identifier for asset inventory and cross-scan correlation.

capabilities.name: rockwell_pccc_execute_pccc
capabilities.description: Rockwell/Allen-Bradley PLCs expose the legacy PCCC command set via CIP service 0x4B (Execute PCCC) on class 0x67 — supports memory-file reads (protected-typed-logical-read) with NO auth, dumping tag values, program state, and controller password hash from a MicroLogix/SLC/PLC-5 target.
capabilities.protocol_reference: Rockwell 1756-PM020/PM021 (PCCC / DF1 Protocol and Command Set), CIP Vol 2 Ch. 6 (Vendor-Specific Extensions)

capabilities.name: cip_stop_cpu_service
capabilities.description: Unauthenticated Stop/Start via Identity-Object Reset (service 0x05) or the Rockwell Modify Mode service (PCCC 0x80 sub 0x01/0x02) drops a running PLC into Program mode from the network — process-halting critical impact, no creds required on any pre-CIP-Security firmware.
capabilities.protocol_reference: ODVA Vol 1 §5-2.2 (Identity Object Reset service 0x05); Rockwell 1756-PM020 (Change Mode 0x8005)

capabilities.name: cip_forward_open_routing
capabilities.description: ForwardOpen (service 0x54) on the Connection Manager (class 0x06) with a padded EPATH lets us route explicit messages through a rack backplane — chassis slot 0..N discovery reveals CPUs, I/O modules and comms cards on the isolated OT bus behind this gateway, extending the surface deeper than the visible IP.
capabilities.protocol_reference: ODVA Vol 1 §3-5.5 (Connection Manager 0x06, ForwardOpen 0x54); Vol 1 App. C (EPATH Routing)
capabilities.notes: Emits new relay_targets (chassis-slot pseudo-hosts) that feed the next scan tranche.

capabilities.name: cip_firmware_download_probe
capabilities.description: Vendor-specific File Object (class 0x37) / Rockwell firmware-download service 0x4E answers 'supported' on many models with no auth — actual write is destructive, but the availability check alone (a GetAttribute on Instance 0xC8) is a critical finding: firmware-flash from the network with no cert or password.
capabilities.protocol_reference: ODVA Vol 1 §5-46 (File Object 0x37); Rockwell CVE-2021-22681 / ICSA-21-056-03 (firmware auth bypass class)

capabilities.name: vendor_id_cve_correlation
capabilities.description: Map (vendor_id, product_code, revision) from Identity Object against the ODVA vendor-ID registry and known-vulnerable-device catalog (Rockwell ICSA advisories, Omron NX/NJ, Siemens 6ES7 CP343-1 EIP, Schneider M580) to emit specific CVE-bound findings — e.g. Rockwell CompactLogix rev < 32 = CVE-2021-22681 (weak session key).
capabilities.protocol_reference: ODVA 'CIP Vendor IDs' registry (odva.org); ICS-CERT ICSA-YY-XXX-NN advisories

capabilities.name: cip_security_negotiation
capabilities.description: Test whether the device rejects plaintext RegisterSession when only CIP Security (DTLS/TLS to Object class 0x5D) is required — a device that accepts unencrypted sessions on 44818 has CIP Security disabled, the single most important OT hardening control.
capabilities.protocol_reference: ODVA Vol 8 (CIP Security), §3.3 (EtherNet/IP Confidentiality Profile) — TCP/2221 (TLS) & UDP/2221 (DTLS) endpoints

capabilities.name: udp_io_class1_listener
capabilities.description: Presence of UDP/2222 open (Class 1 implicit I/O) means real-time process I/O packets traverse this segment in cleartext — a segmentation finding on its own, and lets an attacker sniff/forge I/O assemblies to spoof sensor values without ever touching the PLC on 44818.

capabilities.name: enip_encap_fingerprint_marker
capabilities.description: Signature-detect the fixed 24-byte EtherNet/IP encapsulation header (command LE, length LE, session, status, sender-context, options) in banner/servicefp output to positively ID the port even when nmap returns 'unknown' or 'tcpwrapped' — feeds svcdetect layer 1.

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_hostnames — TCP/IP Interface Object attribute 6 (Host Name) is a fully qualified device name pulled with no auth; feeds DNS/AD correlation.
known_domains — TCP/IP Interface Object attribute 5 (Domain Name) discloses the customer's AD/site domain (very common on Rockwell FactoryTalk-attached PLCs).
known_hostnames — Identity Object attribute 7 (Product Name) frequently embeds the vendor-assigned host label ('CLX-Line5-North') users also configure in DNS.

relay_targets — new surface: backplane chassis slots discovered via ForwardOpen routing (rack IP + slot 0..17) become their own scan targets for the next tranche; recommends a new shared surface 'cip_backplane_targets'.

known_macs (NEW SURFACE) — Ethernet Link Object attribute 4 (Interface MAC) is a hardware-durable identifier worth a shared table so ARP/DHCP/802.1X findings on other services can cross-reference the same box.

ot_asset_inventory (NEW SURFACE) — (vendor_id, device_type, product_code, revision, serial) tuples form a first-class OT asset table; Modbus, S7 (port 102), BACnet and DNP3 modules would populate the same store, giving reports one unified PLC/HMI/drive inventory instead of per-protocol islands.
known_vendor_ids — feeds CVE mapper directly: vendor_id 0x0001 (Rockwell), 0x002F (Omron), 0x005A (Schneider) plus product_code narrows to a single firmware family for ICS-CERT advisory correlation.
known_domains — Identity Object status word / Rockwell PCCC $50/$51 reads can expose the FactoryTalk directory name, another AD-adjacent domain worth wiring to LDAP/Kerberos scans.

existing_coverage.notes: Zero coverage. Grep for 44818/2222/enip/ethernet.ip/cip/ListIdentity across recce/ returns no service-code hits — only unrelated 'cipher' matches. svcdetect.PORT_NAMES has 102 (Siemens S7) and 502 is handled by modbus.py, but 44818 is absent; serviceenum._NAME and _PORT have no ODVA mapping. There is no recce/services/enip.py or recce/services/ethernetip.py.

implementation_notes: Model on recce/services/modbus.py — near-identical shape: single-file module, one probe() function returning a dict, findings()/runbook()/analyze() glue, stdlib socket + struct only (airgap-safe). Key protocol quirks: (1) EtherNet/IP encapsulation header is little-endian, unlike Modbus/TCP's big-endian MBAP — do NOT copy modbus's '>' struct format; use '<HHIIQI' for command/length/session/status/context(8B)/options. (2) List Identity works over both UDP/44818 (broadcast-friendly) and TCP/44818 (connect+read) — try UDP first (no session, single round-trip), fall back to TCP. (3) Every 'active' CIP request beyond List Identity/Services/Interfaces requires a RegisterSession first — cache the session handle and always UnregisterSession in a finally block, or the target counts stale sessions and can DoS itself (Rockwell has a 128-session cap on many models). (4) Never send ForwardClose without a matching ForwardOpen and never send Reset (service 0x05) to Identity Object — it will actually stop the CPU; the capability above is a *supported-service* probe (GetAttribute on the service list attr), not the write itself. Gate exploit-kind capabilities behind an --enable-exploit flag the same way sessions/exploit are gated today. Reuse svcprobe.iter_probe for the target loop and svccommon.findings_to_vulns for the export path — the same wiring modbus.py already uses. Add 44818 to svcdetect.PORT_NAMES (('ethernetip','ODVA EtherNet/IP / CIP')) and add an encapsulation-header signature to _SIGNATURES so nmap-unknown ports get labelled; add 'ethernetip'->'enip' to serviceenum._NAME and 44818->'enip' to _PORT.

recommended_findings.title: EtherNet/IP device reachable on the scanned network
EtherNet/IP identity disclosed (vendor, product, firmware, serial)
CIP TCP/IP object exposes host name, domain and DNS servers
CIP Ethernet Link object exposes MAC address
CIP backplane routable — additional modules reachable via ForwardOpen
Rockwell PCCC (service 0x4B) enabled — unauthenticated memory read/write
Unauthenticated CPU stop/reset capable (Identity Reset service 0x05 or PCCC Change Mode)
Unauthenticated firmware download service exposed (File Object 0x37 / vendor 0x4E)
CIP Security disabled — plaintext explicit messaging accepted on 44818
EtherNet/IP Class 1 implicit I/O traffic exposed on UDP/2222
Known-vulnerable ODVA firmware (vendor/product/revision matches ICS-CERT advisory)

summary: EtherNet/IP is ODVA's adaptation of the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) over TCP/UDP 44818, with real-time I/O on UDP 2222; it is the native fieldbus for Rockwell/Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix/MicroLogix PLCs and is widely deployed in manufacturing, water/wastewater and building automation. An attacker who reaches port 44818 can obtain a full device fingerprint (vendor, product code, firmware, serial, host name, MAC, IP config) with no authentication via List Identity (0x63) and CIP Identity/TCP-IP/Ethernet-Link objects; with a RegisterSession handle they can route explicit messages across the chassis backplane to reach otherwise-isolated modules, execute legacy PCCC commands against Rockwell PLCs, and — on any device without CIP Security — stop the CPU, reset it, or upload firmware, all unauthenticated. Recce currently has zero coverage: svcdetect does not know port 44818, serviceenum has no mapping, and there is no enip.py module. Adding one modelled on modbus.py gives recce a first-class OT-discovery surface that pairs with the existing modbus/S7 coverage and populates a new cross-service OT asset inventory.
